theory.intro: Large numbers can be divided by splitting them into parts that each divide evenly by the divisor, then adding the part-quotients.
facts: Partition the dividend into easy multiples of the divisor.
Choose parts that the divisor goes into without remainder where possible.
steps: Break the number into convenient multiples of the divisor. These may be separate place-value parts or other useful parts.
Divide each part by the divisor.
Add the part-quotients for the answer.

workedExamples.question_text:
Calculate by partitioning:
(a) $969\div3$ into place-value parts
(b) $1836\div6$ into convenient multiples.

A student starts $4284\div7$ by splitting $4284$ into $4000+284$.
(a) Explain why this is unhelpful.
(b) Choose useful parts and calculate.
(c) Show a different useful partition giving the same answer.
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) $4000$ is not divisible by $7$, so this part is not easy to divide exactly.
(b) $4284=4200+84$.
$4284\div7=(4200\div7)+(84\div7)$
$=600+12$
$=612$
(c) $4284=3500+700+84$.
$4284\div7=(3500\div7)+(700\div7)+(84\div7)$
$=500+100+12$
$=612$
Both partitions total $4284$ and all their parts divide exactly by $7$.

workedExamples.question_text:
Four identical event passes cost $3268$ points altogether.
(a) Find the cost of one pass by repeated halving.
(b) Check by partitioning.
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) Divide by $2$, then by $2$ again.
$3268\div2=1634$.
$1634\div2=817$.
One pass costs $817$ points.
(b) $3268\div4=(3200\div4)+(68\div4)$
$=800+17$
$=817$ points, the same answer.
